title: Support/resistance zones — non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's full review of PR #147 (backend-support-resistance), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: Efficiency: `detect_support_resistance_zones` (app/signals/support_resistance.py) runs the full O(n) break/false-breakout scan (`_scan_breaks_and_false_breakouts`) and the `_dollar_volume` window computation for every candidate cluster before sorting by `strength_score` and truncating to `max_zones` (15) -- even though the sort key only depends on the cheap `length_category`/`height_category`. A ~20-year daily history produces ~104 candidate clusters while only 15 are ever returned, so most of that scan work is thrown away on every GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis call for a long-history ticker. Consider scoring/sorting candidates first and only running the expensive scan on the top `max_zones` survivors.

docs/architecture/Backend.md §2's module-layout tree wasn't updated to list the new app/signals/support_resistance.py module under signals/, unlike prior tasks that added a new module to this same list (e.g. indicators/autoenvelope.py, indicators/_validation.py). Add it.

_cluster_touches's sequential merge-by-running-mean can chain: each new point is compared against the cluster's current (shifting) mean rather than its original anchor, so an unbroken sequence of touches each within 1% of the running mean can end up spanning noticeably more than 1% end-to-end. Not a bug (upper/lower are still the cluster's actual price extremes), but this known limitation of naive sequential 1-D clustering isn't acknowledged in the task's decisions entry (which only compares against k-means/density alternatives on complexity/auditability grounds). Consider documenting this explicitly or tightening to an anchor-based tolerance check.
